gaps.sentence: He ___ me his car for the weekend.
gaps.explanation: Offer takes the double-object pattern (offer somebody something); the others do not.

gaps.sentence: 'I will always love you,' he whispered. He whispered that he ___ always love me.
gaps.explanation: Will backshifts to would; 'you' shifts to 'me' from the speaker's new perspective.

gaps.sentence: She ___ me not to worry about the deadline.
gaps.hint: tell sb not to do sth
gaps.explanation: Only 'tell' takes a personal object + not to + infinitive; 'said me not to' is impossible.

gaps.sentence: 'I'll see you tomorrow,' he said. He said he would see me ___.
gaps.explanation: Time expressions shift: tomorrow becomes the next day / the following day.

gaps.sentence: 'Why hasn't she replied?' he wondered. He wondered why she ___ replied.
gaps.explanation: hasn't replied → hadn't replied: statement order and past perfect.

gaps.sentence: 'Don't touch the thermostat,' the technician warned us. The technician warned us ___ the thermostat.
gaps.explanation: Negative commands are reported with 'warned + object + not to + infinitive'.

gaps.sentence: 'We may be a few minutes late,' they warned. They warned that they ___ be a few minutes late.
The colonel ___ his soldiers to advance at dawn.
gaps.explanation: Order + object + to-infinitive reports a command; suggest and hope do not take object + infinitive.
